solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The nouveaux riches on horseback getting over jumps

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a rider who is mounted is said to be up
starts are sudden jumps of surprise

explanation.surface: Newly wealthy people take up riding and show off clearing fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' puts UP above STARTS in this down entry. 'jumps' is a noun here, as in jumps of fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstarts are people who have risen suddenly in wealth or rank, which is what nouveaux riches are.

clue.text: Trap kick on football pitch

definitions.meaning: to trap them with no way out
a set kick taken from the quadrant by the flag

explanation.surface: A trick play at a football match, catching the defence out from a set piece.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pin someone in; as a noun it is the football set kick from the pitch's angle.

clue.text: Nothing in watering hole for pig

indicators.note: the letter for nothing goes into the word for the watering hole

parts.note: a watering hole is slang for a bar
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A pig turns up in a pub with nothing to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A boar is a male pig, or a wild pig.

clue.text: Gloomy, ordinary seaman on board again

indicators.note: being on board a ship means being inside it, so the seaman goes within the other word

parts.note: more, as in 'once more', means again

explanation.surface: A sailor is miserable at being back on the ship once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' signals insertion: the seaman goes inside the word for again, as a sailor is inside a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose is a synonym for sullen and gloomy.

clue.text: Elected, one inside gains new badge of office

parts.note: a party that is elected is in

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed within the rearranged letters
the letters of gains are made into something new

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newly elected official, once in post, gains a badge of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the five letters to SIGNA, and 'inside' places the numeral one within them to give SIGNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are emblems or badges showing rank or office.

clue.text: Writer, crossing street, finds restaurant

indicators.note: the writer word spans across the street abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes

explanation.surface: An author walks over the road and comes upon a place to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author but is a pen: BIRO, a British brand name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant.

clue.text: Soldiers, last in ward, get better

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for soldiers

indicators.note: take the final letter of the word ward

explanation.surface: Wounded troops, last to be admitted to the hospital ward, recover.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to heal or recover from illness.

clue.text: Boo porn that's given out free in US

indicators.note: the letters are dealt out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeer at pornography being distributed without charge in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro bono work, chiefly an American legal term, is done without charge for the public good.

clue.text: One is blown, producing sound

indicators.note: the words are blown apart and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A wind instrument being played makes music.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is a general word for any sound, especially a loud one.

clue.text: Singing voice of cute northerner

indicators.note: the letters come out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A charming man from the north has a lovely voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor is the highest natural adult male singing voice.

clue.text: Old hand English duke failed to mention

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: An ageing aristocrat's role went unrecorded.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out of an account has been skipped or not stated.

clue.text: Country retreat housing a member of the clergy

parts.note: rural means of the country

indicators.note: the retreat word holds the letter A within it

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A vicar has a hideaway in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Church of England a rural dean is a priest overseeing a group of parishes.

clue.text: A cosmetic paste applied under cheek

indicators.note: in a down answer the paste word goes below the cheek word

parts.note: lip is impudence, as in 'none of your lip'
to stick is to paste something on

explanation.surface: Make-up cream is dabbed on beneath the cheekbone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' means insolence, not the face; 'applied under' puts STICK below LIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is a colouring cosmetic for the lips, sold in a stick.

clue.text: Available? Not here

definitions.meaning: a book or record that has been released is available
someone away from home or the office is not in

explanation.definitionFit: The word means released to the public, and also absent or away.

clue.text: Industrial region, seediest, for redevelopment

indicators.note: the letters are rebuilt in a new order, like a site being redeveloped

explanation.surface: A run-down industrial area is earmarked for regeneration.
explanation.definitionFit: Teesside is the area of north-east England around the River Tees, known for steel and chemical works.

clue.text: Group starts to sketch Eiffel Tower

indicators.note: take the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A party of artists begins drawing the Paris landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a collection or group of things or people belonging together.

clue.text: Special gift, article left in shelter

indicators.note: the article and the abbreviation go into the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is a canvas shelter
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A present has been left behind in the tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent is a natural aptitude, often described as a gift.

clue.text: Long pub drink containing very soft fruit

parts.note: to pine is to long for something

indicators.note: the drink word holds the musical abbreviation within it

parts.note: ale is beer served in a pub
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft

explanation.surface: A tall pub cocktail with a mushy piece of fruit in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the drink but is the verb PINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pineapple is a large tropical fruit with a spiky rind.

clue.text: Pointer in joint without lead, led out

indicators.note: the joint word loses its leading letter

parts.note: the knee is a leg joint

indicators.note: the letters of led are put out of order

explanation.surface: A dial's hand inside a pipe joint, with no lead, is taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without lead' drops K from KNEE to give NEE; 'out' rearranges LED to DLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is the pointer on a gauge or compass.

clue.text: Hat in canal

definitions.meaning: a lightweight straw hat named after the Central American country
the shipping canal linking the Atlantic and Pacific

explanation.definitionFit: It is a woven straw hat and also the name of the famous Central American canal.

clue.text: Range of colours spread across permit

indicators.note: the spread word stretches across the permit word, enclosing it

parts.note: pâté is a savoury spread
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A wide array of shades is spread over a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a verb but is a noun, the savoury paste; 'across' has it enclose the permit word.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the range of colours an artist uses, named after the board they mix on.

clue.text: Father, key church leader

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A priest holds the key role as head of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope is head of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Having bosun at sea is a plus

indicators.note: being all at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship's officer aboard is an asset on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra benefit or advantage, something counted as a plus.

clue.text: Cook from Derbyshire town, not well

indicators.note: the word well is taken away from the town's name

parts.note: Bakewell is a market town in Derbyshire, famous for its tart

explanation.surface: A chef from a Peak District town is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: BAKEWELL is a town in Derbyshire, an English county; 'not well' removes WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To bake is to cook food in an oven.

clue.text: Lose one's nerve parking? I can, unfortunately

parts.note: P is the road sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: the letters land badly and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous driver insists they can park but sadly cannot.
explanation.definitionFit: To panic is to be overcome by sudden fear and lose one's composure.

clue.text: With great enthusiasm, similar to mother and daughter

parts.note: like means similar to
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A daughter resembles her mother in being keen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means energetically or furiously, doing something with great vigour.
